expectedText:
HOME CARE AIDE REGISTRY — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS HOME CARE AIDE REGISTRY INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California law governing the Home Care Aide Registry, established under the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (Health and Safety Code Sections 1796.10 through 1796.70) and administered by the State Department of Social Services. It states facts about who must be listed on the registry before providing home care services, the licensing requirement for a business that arranges those services, the background-check and training steps involved, and a licensed home care organization's own duties toward its affiliated home care aides. Acme, Inc. is considering Jordan T. Reyes for the position of Home Care Aide. This document does not determine whether that specific position, or Acme, Inc.'s own business, falls within this chapter's definitions, whether any statutory exclusion applies, or whether Jordan T. Reyes has in fact been listed on the registry; it also does not address the separate general Live Scan / DOJ fingerprint background-check framework (Penal Code Section 11105.3) or the In-Home Supportive Services program, both covered elsewhere in this corpus or excluded from this chapter by its own terms.

AN AFFILIATED HOME CARE AIDE MUST BE LISTED ON THE REGISTRY BEFORE PROVIDING SERVICES
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.14(b) requires an individual who is employed by a home care organization to provide home care services to a client — an "affiliated home care aide" — to be listed on the department-maintained Home Care Aide Registry before providing those services to a client.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "An affiliated home care aide shall be listed on the home care aide registry prior to providing home care services to a client."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.14(b) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, registry listing required before an affiliated home care aide provides services (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.14.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (b) of Section 1796.14. Subdivisions (c) and (d) of the same section list categories of individuals this chapter's "home care aide" definition does not reach at all — including people providing services through a licensed home health agency, hospice, or health facility, an In-Home Supportive Services provider, certain community care, residential care, or child day care licensees, a clinic, a home medical device retail facility, certain regional-center-vendored providers, an alcoholism or drug recovery facility, specified Indian Child Welfare Act placements, and a nonrelative extended family member as defined elsewhere in state law — none of which this clause restates or applies to a particular arrangement.

ARRANGING HOME CARE SERVICES REQUIRES A HOME CARE ORGANIZATION LICENSE
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.35(a) states that, subject to statutory exceptions, an individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, joint venture, association, or other entity may not arrange for the provision of home care services by a registered home care aide to a client in California before obtaining a home care organization license under this chapter, and that doing so without a license is deemed "unlicensed home care services."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "an individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, joint venture, association, or other entity shall not arrange for the provision of home care services by a registered home care aide to a client in this state before obtaining a license pursuant to this chapter. This shall be deemed “unlicensed home care services.”"
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.35(a) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, license required to arrange home care services (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.35.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a). Subdivisions (b) through (d) of the same section describe the department's enforcement response to a violation — a written notice of noncompliance, a civil penalty of $900 per day per violation, referral to the Attorney General or a district attorney or city attorney, and the availability of a cease-and-desist order or an unfair-competition-law action — none of which this clause restates. The quoted text also cross-references exceptions set out in Section 1796.17, which this document does not separately address, and this clause does not determine whether any particular arrangement meets the statutory definition of "arrang[ing] for the provision of home care services."

CRIMINAL-HISTORY REVIEW AS PART OF A HOME CARE AIDE REGISTRATION APPLICATION
In deciding whether to approve a home care aide's registration application, Health and Safety Code Section 1796.19(a)(2) directs the department to consider evidence that the applicant is of reputable and responsible character, including a review of the applicant's criminal offender record information conducted under Health and Safety Code Section 1522 or 1522.7.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Evidence satisfactory to the department that the home care aide applicant is of reputable and responsible character. The evidence shall include, but is not limited to, a review of the independent home care aide applicant’s criminal offender record information pursuant to Section 1522 or 1522.7."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.19(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, criminal-history review as a registration-approval factor (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.19.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only paragraph (2) of a four-paragraph, non-exclusive list of factors the department "shall consider" under Section 1796.19(a); paragraphs (1), (3), and (4) address the applicant's general ability to comply with the chapter, prior revocations or pending disciplinary action related to the care of individuals, and other unspecified information the department may consider, none of which this clause restates. This clause also does not restate the separate substantive standards Sections 1522 and 1522.7 themselves set for what criminal history disqualifies an applicant, and does not determine the outcome of any particular applicant's background review.

A HOME CARE ORGANIZATION'S DUTY TO CONFIRM REGISTRY CLEARANCE BEFORE CLIENT CONTACT
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.43(a) states that a home care organization that employs affiliated home care aides must ensure those aides are cleared on the Home Care Aide Registry before placing them in direct contact with clients.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Home care organizations that employ affiliated home care aides shall ensure the affiliated home care aides are cleared on the home care aide registry before placing the individual in direct contact with clients."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.43(a) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, home care organization's duty to clear affiliated aides before client contact (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.43.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the opening sentence of subdivision (a). The same subdivision goes on, in paragraph (1), to extend a parallel pre-contact clearance requirement (referencing Sections 1796.23 through 1796.28) to "any staff person, volunteer, or employee of a home care organization" with client contact or access to confidential client information, and in paragraph (2) requires a tuberculosis-free demonstration under a separate section; neither is restated here. Subdivision (b), which allows a licensee to require a criminal-record clearance for an individual exempt from this section who nonetheless has client contact, is also not addressed.

MINIMUM ENTRY-LEVEL TRAINING BEFORE AN AFFILIATED HOME CARE AIDE IS PRESENT WITH A CLIENT
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.44(b), as currently in effect, requires an affiliated home care aide to complete a minimum of five hours of entry-level training before being present with a client: two hours of orientation training on the aide's role and the applicable terms of employment, and three hours of safety training covering basic safety precautions, emergency procedures, and infection control. Subdivision (a) places the responsibility for ensuring this occurs on the licensee.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "An affiliated home care aide shall complete a minimum of five hours of entry-level training prior to presence with a client, as follows: (1) Two hours of orientation training regarding their role as home care aide and the applicable terms of employment. (2) Three hours of safety training, including basic safety precautions, emergency procedures, and infection control."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.44(b) (California Legislative Information text, currently operative version), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, entry-level training required before presence with a client (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&division=2.&title=&part=&chapter=13.&article=8.)
  Known gap: Section 1796.44 currently exists in two chaptered versions. The version quoted here is the one operative now: it states, by its own terms, that it "shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027," per amendments made by Stats. 2025, Ch. 414, Sec. 1. A second, already-enacted version of the same section becomes operative January 1, 2027 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 414, Sec. 2); the five-hour entry-level breakdown quoted here is identical in both versions, but the later version adds "the special care needs of clients with dementia" as an additional required topic within the section's separate five-hour annual-training requirement (subdivision (c)), which this clause does not quote or analyze. Because this section has more than one enacted version, its individual leginfo.legislature.ca.gov citation page redirects to a version-selection page rather than displaying text directly; the citation url below instead points to the full chapter-13, article-8 text display, from which the quoted subdivision (b) language was independently confirmed against two separately fetched copies.

TUBERCULOSIS EXAMINATION AS A CONDITION OF EMPLOYMENT AS AN AFFILIATED HOME CARE AIDE
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.45(a) requires an affiliated home care aide hired on or after January 1, 2016, to submit to an examination for active tuberculosis disease either 90 days before employment begins or within seven days after it begins. Subdivision (e) states that this examination is a condition of both initial and continuing employment with the home care organization.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Affiliated home care aides hired on or after January 1, 2016, shall submit to an examination 90 days prior to employment, or within seven days after employment, to determine that the individual is free of active tuberculosis disease."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.45(a) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, tuberculosis examination timing for a newly hired affiliated home care aide (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.45.)
  "The examination is a condition of initial and continuing employment with the home care organization."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.45(e) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, tuberculosis examination as a condition of employment (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.45.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivisions (a) and (e). Subdivision (b) defines "examination" (a CDC-recommended, FDA-licensed infection test, followed by a chest X-ray if positive) and states an aide may not work unless the licensee obtains documentation of no risk of spreading the disease; subdivision (c) requires retesting at least every two years unless a positive test has already been followed by an X-ray; subdivision (d) requires the aide to submit, and the organization to keep on file, an examining practitioner's certificate; and subdivision (f) allows an aide transferring between home care organizations to satisfy the requirement by producing or having verified a certificate from within the past two years. None of those subdivisions is restated here.

A HOME CARE AIDE'S REGISTRATION MUST BE RENEWED EVERY TWO YEARS
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.31(a)(1) requires a registered home care aide to renew registration every two years to remain on the Home Care Aide Registry, with the registration expiring on the anniversary of the initial registration date if not timely renewed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "To remain on the home care aide registry, a registered home care aide shall renew his or her registration every two years."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.31(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, biennial renewal of home care aide registration (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.31.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the opening sentence of paragraph (1) of subdivision (a). The remainder of paragraph (1), and paragraph (2), describe the mechanics of requesting renewal (submitting a renewal application form and paying a nonrefundable fee before the expiration date) and the consequence of a late renewal (forfeiture under Section 1796.26(b)); subdivision (b)'s multi-part list of conditions on which renewal itself is conditioned was not reviewed for this clause. This clause does not state what those renewal conditions are or resolve any particular aide's renewal status.

A HOME CARE ORGANIZATION MUST NOTIFY THE DEPARTMENT WHEN AN AFFILIATED AIDE'S EMPLOYMENT ENDS
Health and Safety Code Section 1796.43(a)(3) requires a home care organization to immediately notify the department when it no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Immediately notify the department when the home care organization no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1796.43(a)(3) (California Legislative Information text), Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act, notice to the department when affiliated-aide employment ends (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1796.43.)
  Known gap: This is one of three duties enumerated in Section 1796.43(a); the other two (pre-contact clearance under paragraph (1) and tuberculosis-status confirmation under paragraph (2)) are addressed in a separate clause of this document. The statutory text quoted here does not define "immediately" in days or hours, does not specify a required notification method or form, and does not state a penalty for a late or missed notification; this document does not address the department's enforcement provisions found elsewhere in this chapter.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding California's Home Care Aide Registry requirements was reviewed by Acme, Inc. regarding Jordan T. Reyes's prospective position of Home Care Aide on September 8, 2026. It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked in each authority section above and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.

Reviewed by (on behalf of Acme, Inc.): ______________________
Date: September 8, 2026
